about.description: Run Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, and Grok CLIs in parallel — approve every session from one browser tab, even from your phone.
about.head: 4e771a5

name: v0.11.1
body:
(The `v0.11.0` tag published nothing: its release run stopped at the macOS and
Linux native builds, before signing. The fix is listed under Fixed.)

### Added

- **The slash-command picker now works with Devin CLI sessions.** Sessions
  launched as a `devin-cli` custom provider get a bundled command list
  (fetched from the repository's `devin-cli.md` source, overridable in
  Settings → Slash command sources) plus locally discovered Devin skills
  from the Devin, Cognition and `.agents` skill directories. Single-line
  inputs starting with `/` are sent as bracketed paste with a deferred
  Enter so Devin's own completion popup no longer swallows the first
  Enter and leaves commands half-typed.

- **You can see and pause the board taker on this PC.** On a Hub with
  `local_taker` in `board.json`, a header button shows whether the taker is
  working (green dot), paused (yellow) or waiting. Its dialog shows the run in
  progress, today's count against the daily limit and the next look at the
  board, and has a Pause / Resume switch: while paused no new work is taken (a
  run already going finishes), and it stays paused across Hub restarts. Recent
  runs are listed with their result, and "Show what it did" opens the run's
  steps — what claude said, the commands it ran and their output — kept on this
  PC under `~/.many-ai-cli/logs/local-taker/` (secrets masked, newest 50 runs).
  With desktop notifications on, the dashboard tells you when a run starts and
  when it ends. The board still holds the request and its result; this keeps
  only how the run went on this machine, under the board's request id.

- **The sidebar tabs can sit in a vertical rail.** A new "Sidebar tabs" choice
  in Settings → Layout switches the tab strip from one horizontal row to a
  narrow rail on the left of the session cards. Reordering tabs, dropping a
  card or a project onto a tab, and the right-click menu work the same way;
  the arrow keys switch to Up/Down. It applies only at mouse-driven PC widths
  (721px and up) — phone widths and touch screens keep the horizontal strip.
  The default stays horizontal, and the choice is stored in this browser only.
- **Quick command buttons can show a custom label.** Each quick command slot
  takes an optional short label (up to 12 characters, counting emoji as one)
  that is shown on the button instead of the truncated command. The label can
  be set in the quick-command settings list and in the edit dialog, and the
  right-click menu shows it next to the command so you can tell which button it
  is. Leaving it blank keeps the truncated command, as before.
- **A registered AI CLI can receive the approval rules.** A provider definition
  that sets `capabilities.agents_md_instructions` to `true` (for a CLI that
  reads the project's `AGENTS.md` as always-on rules, such as Devin CLI) gets
  the short approval-rules block in the project `AGENTS.md` while its session
  runs. Without it nothing is written, as before. Until now such a CLI was
  never told the approval format, so it asked through its own picker and no
  approval button appeared.
- **Board sync follows a board with safe resumption.** When the board answers
  `board_accept_handoff` with the run's `handoff.generation` (Many Iris), work
  taken with the same key is written as that run: events through
  `board_progress_handoff`, item updates with the run's `request_id` and
  `generation`, a `board_heartbeat_handoff` every 10 minutes while the
  `local_taker` run or the session started from the handed-over list is going,
  and the end through `board_complete_handoff`. Without it such a board refuses
  the writes of the writer that took the work. A board without generations is
  written to as before. See `docs/manual_board-sync.md`.
- **Each AI CLI row in the install/update list has an "Include in updates"
  switch.** It flips only `update.enabled` of that AI CLI's definition, so an AI
  CLI left out of "Update all" can be turned back on without opening settings.
- **A registered AI CLI can now offer the approval-mode picker too.** A
  provider definition's `launch.permission_args` maps `plan` / `acceptEdits` /
  `auto` / `bypassPermissions` to that CLI's own flags (for example Devin CLI:
  `--permission-mode accept-edits` / `dangerous`). New Session shows the picker
  with only the mapped modes, and the full-access mode asks for confirmation
  like the built-in CLIs. A definition without the map shows no picker, as before.
- **An AI can now add a new AI CLI with `many-ai-cli provider add`.** `provider
  list`, `provider remove` and `provider test` complete the set, and
  `provider add --help` is written for an AI agent (what to research, what to
  show you, what only you answer). `--approval-option` registers the CLI's own
  approval phrases. When another path adds a CLI, the dashboard shows "<name>
  was added" with an Undo. Removing keeps a `before-delete` history backup, but
  a removed CLI is re-added with `provider add`; restoring a deleted one is not
  supported. A separately installed older `many-ai-cli` on PATH does not have
  these commands; inside a session, use the binary in `MANY_AI_CLI_BIN`.
- **A registered AI CLI can be an `orchestrate spawn --provider` child and a
  relay role.** Any CLI the registry has enabled with a launch definition is
  accepted besides the built-in seven. A headless child needs the CLI's own
  headless definition, and it gets no built-in permission-tier or subscription
  handling.
- **Adding, changing or removing an AI CLI now reaches every open dashboard.**
  The Hub broadcasts the change, so the new-session list and the settings list
  reload in other tabs and devices without F5.
- **Settings → Usage lists every registered AI CLI, in the same order as New
  Session.** The rows come from the provider registry instead of a fixed table,
  so a custom provider such as Devin CLI appears as soon as it is registered.
  Each row links to the provider's usage page (Usage Links settings gained a
  Devin CLI field); the old "unavailable" badges and per-row info tooltips are
  gone — providers that cannot report usage through the CLI are shown as plain
  links, and remaining-quota meters still appear for the CLIs that can.
- **A screen layout preset can put the whole input area on top.** Settings →
  Layout gains a "Screen layout" selector: "Bottom" keeps the current order,
  "Top" moves the complete input area — the progress/button row, the input
  field, and the attachment/usage row — above the terminal on a mouse-operated
  desktop (721px and wider). The slash list, slash picker, prompt-template
  palette and voice bar then open downward, and the approval popup follows to
  the top by default, with "Always bottom" and the side columns still
  selectable. Phone widths and touch-first screens keep the bottom layout.
- **A console-launched Hub can move into the Windows tray with `many-ai-cli
  tray --replace`.** The tray runs `setup`, stops the old console Hub (logged
  as `tray_migration`), starts a detached Hub and reopens the browser, so
  active sessions just reconnect.
- **Settings → Hub can offer "Move Hub to tray".** On a Windows Hub started
  in a console window that has never been set up and has no tray running, the
  section shows the offer; one confirmation migrates the Hub. If external
  exposure is active it is closed first, and a failed check or close cancels
  the switch.
- **A foreground `serve` now prints a one-time tip** — `many-ai-cli setup`
  keeps the Hub running without its console window — only when the launch
  could still move to the tray.

### Changed

- **The approval-rules block written into `AGENTS.md` is now short.** Codex,
  GitHub Copilot, Cursor Agent, Grok and opencode used to get the full rules
  (about 13 KB) in their instruction file. They now get a block under 1,200
  bytes — the Yes/No form, the done form and the path of the full rules — and
  read the full rules from the Hub's own file when they need the other forms.
  An AI CLI with a budget for always-on rules (Devin CLI: 32,768 bytes in
  total) no longer loses the project's own rules while another CLI's session
  runs in the same project. A full block left by an earlier version is
  replaced on the next session start. Claude Code is unchanged (one import
  line).
- Windows の常駐は、通知領域のアイコンではなく、タスクバーの小さい窓で動いていることを示す。窓を閉じると最小化され、Hub は止まらない。
- 設定の切り替え案内、起動時の 1 行ヒント、setup の完了文を、タスクバーの小さい窓の説明に変えた。
- **On Windows, the taskbar window stays sharp at 125 % / 150 % display scaling.** Both executables now carry an application manifest (normal user rights, Windows 10/11, modern controls, DPI aware), and the small taskbar window scales its size and layout with the display and shows the app icon beside its status line.

### Fixed

- **The macOS and Linux builds compile again.** A Windows-only import in the
  taskbar window code broke the macOS and Linux release builds, and the
  release smoke test could be handed the Hub's default port by the OS and
  refuse it. Both are fixed; the Windows build was not affected.

- **The child spawn confirmation now lets you pick the subscription profile.**
  When the chosen CLI has two or more enabled profiles, the dialog shows the
  same Subscription field as the derive dialog and the new-session panel, and
  switching CLI swaps in that CLI's profiles. The child launches with the
  chosen profile; leaving it at the default (or a CLI with one profile or
  none, where the field is hidden) sends nothing and launches as before. An
  unknown, disabled or other-CLI profile is refused before the child starts,
  and switching CLI no longer carries over a profile the AI asked for on the
  previous CLI. (#43)
- **An AI CLI registered through the dashboard or API now actually launches.**
  The launcher read only the built-in and `config.yaml` definitions, so a CLI
  in the provider registry was started by its id and failed with "not on
  PATH". It now reads the same layers as the Hub.
- **Approvals in custom AI CLI sessions are detected like the built-in ones.**
  Custom sessions skipped the approval marker, native prompt detection and the
  idle-question check, so a registered CLI's "run this?" never became an
  approval button. As in the frozen Go build, only usage probes and shell
  sessions are excluded now.
- **An AI CLI added from another tab, the API or the command line now shows up
  in the new-session list without reloading the page.** The list is read again
  from the Hub each time it is opened. Before, it was read only when the page
  loaded, so a newly added AI CLI stayed missing until the dashboard was reloaded.
- **The "?" buttons in the new-session form are round and centred again.** They
  had no button style of their own, so the browser's default button squeezed the
  "?" into the lower right of a grey square.
- **Sending selected terminal text to a shell session no longer asks for
  confirmation.** "Send as-is" on the terminal's right-click menu used to open
  the browser's own confirm dialog, which pops up far from the menu and breaks
  the flow. Choosing the item is already an explicit send, so the text now goes
  straight to the session like it does for AI CLI sessions.
